title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three fragments.

(1) End of fragment 91 (A.m. T.I p.17–21). This finishes the 'solutio generalior' begun on p.489.
- Setup on the previous page: p+s=αβ, p−s=εζ, q+r=αγ, q−r=εη, with r:s=f:g and q=hβζ. Euler found that the needed divisibility forces gh=−ff.
- Under gh=−ff, pp+ss becomes 5f⁴ζ⁴−6f³gζ³η+7f²g²ζ²η²−6fg³ζη³+2g⁴η⁴ = (f²ζ²+g²η²)(5f²ζ²−6fgζη+2g²η²).
- The expression to be made a square is λ(5f²ζ²−6fgζη+2g²η²)(f²ζ²+g²η²)(f²η²+h²ζ²) / [hfgη(2hζ−fη)].
- For solvability the two factors f²ζ²+g²η² and f²η²+h²ζ² must 'coalesce', i.e. differ by a square factor. This needs f²:h²=g²:f², which holds automatically because h=−f²/g. Then f²η²+h²ζ² = (f²/g²)(f²ζ²+g²η²).
- Removing squares leaves λ(5f²ζ²−6fgζη+2g²η²)/[fη(fη−2hζ)], or equivalently λ(…)/[gη(2fζ+gη)].
- Euler notes this is just the earlier special solution with ζ,η replaced by fζ,gη. The 'more general' parametrisation gives nothing new; only the ratios matter.

(2) Fragment 92 (J. A. Euler).
- It multiplies two diagonal binary quadratic forms and writes the product again in the shape ab·x²+aβ·y², with x=apr±βqs and y=αps∓bqr.
- This is a composition (Brahmagupta-type) identity for diagonal forms.
- For the cross terms 2a²bβ·pqrs and 2aαbβ·pqrs to cancel, the letter printed α must equal a. The consistent identity is (a²p²+bβq²)(abr²+aβs²) = ab(apr±βqs)² + aβ(aps∓bqr)².

(3) Fragment 93 (Lexell).
- With x³=a, the problem is to find a multiplier px²+qx+r making (fx²+gx+h)(px²+qx+r) rational. This is rationalising, i.e. taking the norm, in the pure cubic field Q(∛a).
- Setting the x² and x coefficients to zero gives the adjugate multiplier and the norm. Correctly: p=fh−g², q=gh−af², r=afg−h², and product = 3afgh − a²f³ − ag³ − h³ = −N(h+gx+fx²).
- The printed text drops a in several places (constant term, p(hg−f²), the final product), so its formula 3fgh−f³−g³−h³ is literally the case a=1.
- Purpose: to run the continued-fraction algorithm for cube roots exactly. Each complete quotient (A+Bx+Cx²)/D is inverted by multiplying by this conjugate.
- Example ∛2 with rough approximations x≈1¼, x²≈1½ (true values 1.26 and 1.587). The text breaks off ('....').
errors: Fragment 93: the reduced product should be (fr+hp+gq)x² + (fpa+gr+hq)x + a(fq+gp) + hr. The printed constant term 'fq+gp+hr' omits the factor a.

Fragment 93: the third relation r=(−fq−gp)/h is spurious. It would make the whole product vanish; only the x² and x coefficients must vanish. Writing '=0' for the reduced product is likewise incorrect.

Fragment 93: from hpg+g²q=f²pa+fhq one gets p(hg−af²)=q(fh−g²), not p(hg−f²). So q=hg−af², r=afg−h², and the product is 3afgh−a²f³−ag³−h³. The printed formula 3fgh−f³−g³−h³ is valid only for a=1, where x is rational and the problem is trivial.
Fragment 93: x²≈1½ is a poor approximation to ∛4≈1.587 (1⅗ would be better). This is harmless as a starting guess.

Fragment 92: as transcribed (first factor with α, product terms aaαβ pprr, and y=αps∓bqr), the cross terms do not cancel unless α=a. The p²r² coefficient should be a³b. Either Greek α and italic a are confused in print, or there is a misprint.
Fragment 91: computations check (factorisation of pp+ss, coalescence of factors, both reduced forms). No error found.

ideas.what: Two-parameter family for making λ·(pp+ss)(qq+rr)/(…) a square; the generalisation collapses to the special case by rescaling ζ→fζ, η→gη
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of rational points on a quartic/elliptic-type Diophantine condition; equivalence of parametrisations under scaling
ideas.where_published: Similar techniques throughout Euler's Diophantine papers and Algebra II; the specific problem is unsure

ideas.what: Product of two diagonal binary quadratic forms is again of the form ab·x²+aβ·y²
ideas.modern_name: Composition of (diagonal) binary quadratic forms; generalised Brahmagupta–Euler identity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brahmagupta (7th c.), Euler, Lagrange; general composition by Gauss (1801)
ideas.where_published: Euler's Algebra (E387/388) and papers on forms mxx+nyy (e.g. E256, E556); exact form unsure

ideas.what: Rationalising multiplier (adjugate) for fx²+gx+h in Q(∛a), and the norm form
ideas.modern_name: Norm form of a pure cubic field, N(h+gθ+fθ²)=h³+ag³+a²f³−3afgh
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Lagrange (cubic forms, 1760s–70s); later Dirichlet, Eisenstein
ideas.where_published: Euler, Algebra II on irrational expressions with cube roots; Lagrange, Additions to Euler's Algebra (1774) on such norm forms

ideas.what: Using the cubic conjugate to expand ∛2 exactly as a continued fraction
ideas.modern_name: Continued-fraction algorithm for algebraic numbers in exact arithmetic (number-field representation of complete quotients)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (Sur la résolution des équations numériques, 1769; Additions 1774)
ideas.where_published: Lexell's own fragment here; Lagrange's memoirs for the general method

missed.claim: Lexell's computation of the continued fraction of ∛2 via exact conjugate rationalisation breaks off after the setup. Whether the partial quotients of ∛2 are bounded remains open today.
missed.quote: Hujus ope radices cubicas numerorum licebit ad fractiones continuas revocare. ... fractio x/1 in fractionem continuam convertatur....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historically: it documents an early (1770s, Euler circle) attempt to expand a cubic irrational exactly. The open question of bounded partial quotients for real cubic irrationals is well known (e.g. Lang–Trotter 1972), so nothing mathematically new is here.

deep.surprise_reason: All three items are routine: a parametric Diophantine reduction that Euler himself notes gives nothing new, a standard composition identity for diagonal quadratic forms, and the norm/rationalisation in Q(∛a), printed with a dropped. The continued-fraction remark is a minor historical curiosity.
transcription_corrections: Fragment 92: the letter transcribed as α in 'αapp', 'aaαβpprr', 'αappss' and 'y=αps∓bqr' must be italic a (or the print has a misprint) for the identity to hold. The consistent reading is (aapp+bβqq)(abrr+aβss)=ab(apr±βqs)²+aβ(aps∓bqr)².
Fragment 93: the multiplier in the problem statement reads 'pxx+qx+r' (partly obscured at the margin in the scan).

Fragment 93: the formulas lack a where it is mathematically required (constant term a(fq+gp)+hr; p(hg−af²); q=hg−aff; r=afg−hh; product 3afgh−a²f³−ag³−h³). This appears to be an error in the printed text itself, not a transcription error.
